short: The turning point of 1918, where a failed German offensive was met by a massive Allied counterattack that definitively broke the German advance.
full:
Seeking to draw Allied reserves away from Flanders, General Erich Ludendorff launched the final phase of his Spring Offensive on 15 July 1918 along the Marne River. Unlike earlier assaults, this attack was anticipated by the French command, who had established a flexible defense-in-depth supported by robust intelligence. The German vanguard crossed the river but was quickly contained and subjected to devastating artillery fire, halting the offensive within days.

On 18 July, the Allies launched a massive surprise counter-offensive spearheaded by French tanks and fresh American divisions. They tore into the overextended German flanks, forcing a chaotic retreat and eliminating the salient that had threatened Paris. The decisive victory permanently shifted the initiative to the Allies, marking the beginning of the unrelenting sequence of offensives that would ultimately force the collapse of the German Empire.
